o1.biggest_strength: The whole series is built on the two retention habits (recurring task and second device). It skips emails already done, branches on signup platform, and ends with a day-8 email that points each user to the habit they're missing.
o1.biggest_mistake: Success measures are mostly series-level rather than a clear 'worked if' per email. The day-8 email also relies on branching by past behavior, which the tool may not support, and the control group gets no onboarding emails at all.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give each email its own 'worked if' line, make the day-8 branching explicitly rely only on the allowed triggers, and trim to the 1,200-word limit.

o2.biggest_strength: Every email has a trigger, a typed example in quotes, a button, a goal and a baseline-linked 'worked if'. The drop list is detailed with numbers and a sensible plan to bring the team invite back in 2027.
o2.biggest_mistake: The fifth email is a Pro upsell with a Pro-feature claim that wasn't in the brief. It spends the final slot on selling instead of closing the gap on the missing habit, so the series never targets the 67% both-habits group.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Replace the Pro email with a 'the step that's left' email aimed at the missing habit, and cut the length to the 1,200-word limit.

reason: I'd rather have the series that keeps pushing users toward the two habits, ends on the missing one, and moves Pro out of onboarding. The other has cleaner per-email measures, but it spends its last slot on a Pro upsell.
